To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FoxE1 binds in vivo to the promoters of two novel target genes, Nis, and Duox2, and also to the classical thyroid genes Titf1, Nis, Pax 8 and Duox2.
FoxE1 regulates a number of genes, some of them involved in thyroid function and development.

FoxE1 is an important regulator of the thyroid-specific gene Nis, which is involved in the thyroid iodide transport, and of Duox2, which encodes the enzyme responsible for the production of the thyroid-specific oxidants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying novel direct FoxE mutations, which may lead to a better understanding of the molecular basis of thyroid diseases.
the identification of novel FoxE1 targets in thyroid cells, which will be useful for the understanding of thyroid physiology and pathophysiology.
the identification of FoxE1 downstream mediators, providing new insights into its transcriptional networks in normal thyroid cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

FoxE1 plays an important role in the transcriptional regulation of a wide array of genes, including classical thyroid genes such as Tg, Tpo, Nis and Pax8, as well as other thyroid genes such as Nis, Duox2, Adamts9, Casp4, Cdh1 and S100a5.

FoxE1 is involved in the transcriptional regulation of several genes, including the two novel target genes identified in this work, and that this transcriptional network may be relevant for thyroid development and differentiation.
FoxE1 regulates a large number of thyroid genes, which in turn may be involved in thyroid development and/or function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FoxE1 regulates a large number of downstream targets in thyroid cells and that FoxE1 and FoxE1-NF1/CTF co-regulate Nis expression.
FoxE1 regulates a large number of target genes that may be relevant for thyroid development, homeostasis and differentiation.
the thyroid-specific transcriptional network regulated by FoxE1 is much more complex than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the identification of novel downstream mediators of the FoxE transcriptional program will help to clarify the mechanisms involved in thyroid gland development and differentiation, which are crucial for the understanding of endocrine syndroms and thyroid cancer susceptibility.
FoxE1 is not a simple transcriptional regulator of Tg and TPO, but rather a key regulator of the thyroid cell transcriptional program.
FoxE1 plays a central role in thyroid cell homeostasis and differentiation.
